subject: Request for remediation allowance after sustained latency window - exec approval needed
messages:
From: Priya Nair <priya.nair@olivesys.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ravi.sharma@olivesys.ai, legal@olivesys.ai
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent latency window impacting production - evidence attached

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this up. We observed significant tail latency across our inference flows from 2027-05-06 02:00 UTC through 2027-05-08 20:00 UTC. Traffic routes were steady and we reproduced the elevated p95/p99 on our side. This hit two user-facing features and impacted a live campaign.

We need a formal remediation allowance to cover the customer-facing impact (credits and a one-page customer statement). Our procurement team also needs an itemized number we can put on our next invoice reconciliation — ideally a single-line credit and a short commitment to steps you’ll take to avoid recurrence.

Attached are our logs and a short timeline: olivesys_latency_window_20270506-20270508.csv

Can you confirm the remediation you propose and whether you need executive signoff for anything above standard SLA terms?

Priya
Priya Nair
Head of Platform Reliability
Olive Systems

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Nair <priya.nair@olivesys.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent latency window impacting production - evidence attached

Hi Priya —

Really sorry to hear about the impact and thanks for the detailed timeline. We dug into the window and have a few notes:
- Root cause: a combination of a low-probability kernel regress in our batching layer + a misrouted traffic spike that bypassed a prefix cache.
- Scope: roughly 48 hours of elevated p99 for requests with long context (>2k tokens); p50 unaffected.

Proposed remediation offer (subject to exec approval):
- One month of service credit (applied as 100% credit to May invoice) plus,
- A one-time supplementary credit equal to 20% of the impacted-month usage (to recognize lost campaign opportunity), and
- A prioritized postmortem and a rolling patch with a targeted mitigation deployed within 2 weeks.

I’ve attached the offer in spreadsheet form: proposed-remediation-offer.xlsx and a consolidated SLA summary for the window: sla-uptime-summary.pdf.

We believe the combination of a one-month credit + 20% supplemental credit is a reasonable makewhole and keeps the contract terms intact, but anything above that requires exec signoff — specifically any multi-month forgiveness or unusual pricing concessions.

Karthik — can you please review and confirm whether we can approve this as-is, or if you’d prefer we escalate to leadership for an exception?

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent latency window impacting production - evidence attached

Marissa / Lauren —

Thanks for the analysis. A few quick operational and commercial notes before I sign off:
- We should quantify the proposed supplemental credit in dollars for procurement (Priya requested a line item). Marissa, please add the estimated impacted tokens and the dollar equivalent in the spreadsheet.
- We need legal to confirm that the credit wording is limited to "remediation allowance" and does not amend the SLA or create an evergreen pricing change.
- Given Olive is a strategic customer (DEAL-9842) and this was a platform-side regression, I am inclined to support: one month full credit + 25% supplemental (instead of 20%) as a one-off, provided legal signs off and the customer accepts the standard remediation language.

I will approve this offer up to $85,000 total remediation value. Anything above requires a VP-level signoff. If you think this exceeds that cap, escalate to Marissa for exec loop.

If Marissa sends me the revised spreadsheet with the dollar math, I’ll reply by EOD tomorrow.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Nair <priya.nair@olivesys.ai>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, legal@olivesys.ai
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Persistent latency window impacting production - evidence attached

Priya —

Appreciate your patience. Per the internal review, Redwood can offer the following remediation package (one-time, non-precedent setting):

1) One month of service credit applied to your May invoice (100% of recurring fees for one billing month).
2) A supplementary remediation credit equal to 25% of your measured usage during the impact window (we’ve calculated this as $62,350).
3) A short customer-facing incident statement we’ll draft and share for your review.
4) A prioritized engineering patch and a deliverable plan; we’ll run a joint technical review next week.

Total remediation value: $62,350 + one month credit (estimated combined value under the $85,000 executive cap declared by Karthik).

Attachments: proposed-remediation-offer.xlsx (updated with token math and dollar conversions), sla-uptime-summary.pdf, olivesys_latency_window_20270506-20270508.csv

Next steps: If Olive Legal confirms the remediation wording is acceptable, we’ll schedule the joint technical review and apply the credit to your account. Please confirm acceptance or raise any questions by EOD Thursday so we can process for the May invoice.

Thanks again and sorry for the disruption.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
